Base project calculation

See the low, base and high build estimate chart ↓

What supports the total?

Published benchmarks: direct retailer listings, a metal-roof manufacturer's guide and Homewyse's May 2026 national unit-cost estimates. Source dates, scopes and limitations are linked for every priced line. None is represented as a localized quote.

Mixed estimates: framing combines observed lumber prices with an employee wage reference and explicit labor assumptions. Countertop fixed costs include a $200 unverified faucet reserve. Drywall guides overlap jointing supplies; their combined figure requires a package quote.

Unpriced work: no defensible matching unit price was established for 13 construction packages. These packages have explicit unverified cash reserves until matching quotes establish their prices.

Markup: 17.5% is the midpoint of Homewyse's published 13–22% general-contractor add-on guidance (P11). The lower/base/higher scenarios use 13% / 17.5% / 22% by default. Applying these to the whole direct subtotal is a scenario choice. Obtain the builder's actual terms and remove duplication if a quote already includes the same general-contractor charge.

Contingency: The base uses 20%, with 15% lower and 25% higher scenario assumptions reflecting unresolved site conditions, specifications and package prices. It is not a sourced market rate or a statistical confidence allowance.

Project reserves: $20,000 site/utilities, $12,000 design, $7,000 permits and $5,000 tax/extra freight are unverified base cash provisions, varied by the disclosed scenario multipliers. Standard local delivery is already in the Homewyse benchmarks; the freight reserve is for uncovered delivery, not a blanket second delivery fee. Tax treatment needs a jurisdiction and taxable-cost schedule.

How each LF price is derived

Material-only rate

Board price ÷ board length. Example: a listed $10.75, 10 ft 2×6 gives $1.075/LF before waste and tax (P1). That is a material reference, not an installed stud price.

Installed framing component

Material $/LF × 1.10 overage × 1.15 incidentals + worker-hours/LF × $54.60. The $54.60 productive-hour assumption equals the BLS $29.12 employee wage × assumed 1.50 employment burden ÷ assumed 0.80 productive utilization. A stud example uses 0.055 worker-hours/LF: $1.075 × 1.10 × 1.15 + 0.055 × $54.60 = $4.36/LF rounded.

Labor-time assumptions range by member type and are disclosed on selection. The low case uses 70% of base time, a 1.30 burden, 90% utilization and 10% incidentals; the high case uses 150% time, 1.80 burden, 65% utilization and 25% incidentals. These are sensitivity inputs, not measured crew output. U.S. nominal sizes are price proxies for metric concept sections; structural equivalence is not established.

Area-to-length conversion

Installed $/sq ft × relevant surface area ÷ model LF. This preserves the source's area basis while expressing an equivalent cost per model board foot of length. Board width, gaps and cut geometry affect that conversion. The unit is LF, not lumber board feet.

For a continuous countertop, multiply $/sq ft by depth in feet: the retailer's $80/sq ft average × (650 ÷ 304.8) ft depth = $170.60/LF. The $830 fixed sink/cutout/faucet bundle is added separately (P13).

Per-item-to-length conversion

Price per cabinet × four modules ÷ 7.87 LF. The published $486–$736 per-cabinet range has a $611 midpoint; four modules give $310.55/LF rounded (P12). This equivalent applies to this layout only.

Scope boundaries

Roof-panel cost is the installed roofing-package remainder after subtracting the separate trim-material line; all roof labor stays in that package. Deck board pricing excludes supports. Drywall hanging and finishing labor are separate, but their source supplies overlap: no unsupported credit was guessed. Replace both drywall lines with one matched quote.

How sources were used: published headline installed ranges were used directly or converted; base values are arithmetic midpoints except the countertop, which uses the retailer's stated average. No licensed RSMeans rate or local contractor bid was obtained. Inconsistent dollar values in the extracted Homewyse detail tables were not used to invent material/labor splits. Retail listings are observed prices without a project ZIP, not promised availability or delivered prices. No unsupported inflation escalation was applied to older-dated guides.

Unresolved reserves, exclusions and model limits

    What the 3D quantities mean

    Cladding cuts, decking and opening counts are measured from the existing conceptual reconstruction. Added framing is an assumed counting layout. Insulation, sheets, paint and drywall highlights show surfaces or locations, not every physical layer. Pipe and wire routes remain undetermined, so no invented pipe/cable LF is shown. Select a material for its formula and limitations.

    The model was reconstructed from Plana-House-Plans.pdf, issue 02 dated June 6, 2026. Envelope assumptions are 12.25 × 4.15 m, 2.625 m wall height and a 45° roof with 0.10 m overhangs. Unit conversions: 1 ft = 0.3048 m; 1 sq ft = 0.09290304 m². Quantities have not become engineered merely because prices are now sourced.

    Still excluded: land, finance/carrying costs, property taxes, demolition, extraordinary excavation/retaining work, unusually long utilities/driveways, new well/septic, solar/batteries, loose furniture and major redesign. Local code, room-size, egress, structural and energy requirements may change scope; the small second bedroom in the concept remains unresolved. Requirements for excluded work increase the budget.

    Needed to localize: country/city or ZIP, site and soil information, engineered framing/foundation schedule, selected roof/cladding/windows, insulation targets and a complete MEP specification. Price matches must include the same scope, waste, delivery, tax and contractor overhead.
